children: AMMAN: The Jordan Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Fund (JREEEF), affiliated with the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources, on Monday launched a project to install solar photovoltaic systems at public buildings operated by 18 municipalities in southern Jordan.

The project is part of a nationwide programme aimed at expanding the use of renewable energy and improving energy efficiency across municipalities in the Kingdom, the public service broadcaster, Al Mamlaka, reported.
The programme targets 104 municipalities and will see solar systems installed at 188 municipal buildings, with a combined capacity of up to 3.4 megawatts.
The systems are expected to reduce municipalities’ electricity bills by around JD550,000 annually, while cutting carbon dioxide emissions by 3,838 tonnes a year, according to JREEEF.

The programme also includes a capacity-building component under which more than 550 municipal employees will receive training through two specialised training packages. The training is intended to ensure the long-term sustainability of the systems and improve their management, operation and maintenance.
The launch of the phase in the southern region follows the completion of the programme’s work in municipalities in northern Jordan.
Ministry Secretary-General Amani Azzam said that the expansion to the southern region reflects the government’s commitment to extending sustainable energy projects to all parts of the Kingdom.

She said that the project would provide municipalities with practical solutions to help reduce their financial burdens, adding that lower energy costs would allow local authorities to redirect more of their resources towards improving services for citizens.
Azzam described the initiative as a practical example of how renewable energy can support local development while boosting financial and environmental sustainability.

She also highlighted the partnership with Italy’s Ministry of Environment and Energy Security, saying it supports Jordan’s national efforts to advance the energy transition and reduce carbon emissions.

The partnership also places a strong emphasis on developing the skills of municipal employees, enabling them to operate and manage solar energy systems in line with technical standards and the best practices, she said.
JREEEF Executive Director Rasmi Hamza said that the fund was continuing to implement projects targeting priority service and development sectors.
The installation of solar systems in southern municipalities marks an important step in expanding renewable energy applications and improving energy efficiency in public institutions, he said.

Hamza added that JREEEF provides municipalities with the technical, financial and training support needed to ensure the systems remain sustainable and deliver the expected economic and environmental benefits.
He said that the results achieved in northern municipalities would provide important momentum for implementing the project in the southern region efficiently and effectively.
